title: Briefing: France, India, Albania, Italy and South Africa
script: Good morning. It's Thursday, November fifth, and this is the Unowned briefing: the stories that matter, checked and graded. It's read by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our published timelines.
Every item carries our grade. Confirmed means independent outlets agree. Reported means one source so far. Disputed means the accounts conflict. And alleged is one side's claim.
Here are the top stories.
France. Today: Around a dozen Xavier‑Grall teachers wear white armbands, support striking colleagues' demands while school stays open.
India. Today: Union Minister Jitendra Singh alleges Cockroach Janta Party founder received foreign funding, party denies.
Albania. Yesterday: new developments in Albania's student protests.
Italy. Yesterday: Rete degli Studenti Medi coordinator calls for more school funding as students protest for teachers.
South Africa. Yesterday: South African Government says asylum seekers and refugees barred from voting under Refugee Regulations.
Canada. No new developments since Monday, November second.
Germany. No new developments since Monday, November second.
Serbia. No new developments since Monday, November second.
Now the details.

France. Today: Around a dozen teachers at the Xavier‑Grall agricultural high school in Loudéac wore white armbands to show solidarity with striking colleagues on 5 November 2026. The teachers said the gesture signalled support for demands on working conditions and salaries, while the school remained open and classes continued, Ouest‑France reports. Our grade: reported, from a single source so far. Also today: FSU teachers' union said in a video on Instagram that 52% of lower secondary teachers were striking on 5 November, that the strike was widely followed in primary schools and the public sector, and that the union would pursue rapid follow‑up actions with its partners. That's their own claim, posted on their channel, and we grade it alleged.

India. Today: Union Minister Jitendra Singh alleged that the Cockroach Janta Party's founder and co-convenor received foreign funding from US donors and Pakistani politicians, which the party dismissed as baseless claims from officials lacking accountability. PTI and other outlets report. Our grade: alleged. That's a claim by one side that no one has independently confirmed. Coming up: The Special Executive Magistrate hearing for the CJP leaders summoned over the Jantar Mantar protest listed for the third week of November.

Albania. Yesterday, Wednesday, November fourth: Democratic Party of Albania said in an Instagram post that it is ready for protests and calls for Prime Minister Rama to be imprisoned. That's their own claim, posted on their channel, and we grade it alleged.

Italy. Yesterday, Wednesday, November fourth: The national coordinator of the Rete degli Studenti Medi school-student network tells la Repubblica that the government should invest more in schools, and that fewer staff would lower the quality of teaching. Students say they are protesting for teachers as well as for themselves. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, la Repubblica, and isn't yet confirmed by a second. Coming up: The USB union said on Instagram that it will hold a full-day national strike of social cooperative and enterprise workers across Italy on November 16.

South Africa. Yesterday, Wednesday, November fourth: The South African Government said on X, on local-election day, that asylum seekers and refugees may not vote. Its graphics cite the Refugee Regulations, which it says bar them from political activity, and the Electoral Act, which it says limits voting to registered citizens aged 18 or over. That's the authority's own claim, from its official statement, and we grade it alleged until independent reporting backs it up. Coming up: The new asylum appointment system Home Affairs said would be in place by November tenth.
Also on our watch, with no new developments in recent days.

Canada. The latest report, from Monday, November second: Nine British Columbia First Nations announce Federal Court applications to quash the Pacific Link national-interest designation, saying Ottawa did not adequately consult them. Our grade: confirmed by independent reporting.

Germany. The latest report, from Monday, November second: Germany's Education Minister Karin Prien calls the concerns of the young people who marched in more than 30 cities on October thirty-first "legitimate and extremely relevant" and promises more dialogue, and SPD politicians call for a national education summit. We grade that reported: so far only The Local Germany has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.

Serbia. The latest report, from Monday, November second: Serbia's Supreme Public Prosecutor's Office orders the Belgrade prosecutors to act on student complaints against criminal police chief Marko Kričak over an August 2025 incident in a Government of Serbia garage, which had gone more than a year without result, Vreme reports. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, Vreme, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.
We'll bring you updates on those as soon as they become available.

Coming up in the days ahead. Saturday, November fourteenth, Germany: Gen Z regelt plans another countrywide protest on November fourteenth. Sunday, November fifteenth, Canada: Whether binding Pathways carbon-storage agreements are signed by the November fifteenth target.
That's the Unowned briefing for Thursday, November fifth. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com. Thanks for listening.
